record.paper_title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers-Ramanujan-Type Identities. A Survey of Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let C be the A2 Cartan matrix [[2,-1],[-1,2]]. For L=(L1,L2) in Z_+^2 and k=(k1,k2,k3) in Z^3 with k1+k2+k3=0, let S(L,k) be the normalized A2 supernomial S(L,k)=1/(q)_{CL} times the completely antisymmetric supernomial with top vector CL and lower vector L2(1,1,1)-k; the underlying supernomial is the finite Young-diagram-chain sum whose factors are Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. Restrict k to the dominant chamber k1>=k2>=k3 and set K=(k1+k2,k1). Since S(L,K) is nonzero exactly in the range K1<=L1, K2<=L2, 2K1>=K2, 2K2>=K1, 2L1>=L2, and 2L2>=L1, find an explicit closed formula for the inverse matrix Sbar(K,L) satisfying sum_{L1,L2>=0} Sbar(k,L) S(L,k') = delta_{k,k'} and sum_{dominant k, |k|=0} S(L,k) Sbar(k,L') = delta_{L,L'}. Partial formulas are known for K=(r,2r-p) with p=0,1,2,3; the goal is a formula for arbitrary K.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$ be the $A_2$ Cartan matrix. For a vector $v=(v_1,v_2)\in\mathbb Z^2$ write $(q)_v=(q)_{v_1}(q)_{v_2}$, where $(q)_n=\prod_{i=1}^n(1-q^i)$ for $n\ge0$ and $(q)_n=\infty$ for $n<0$. Define the Gaussian $q$-binomial coefficient $\binom{a}{b}_q=(q)_a/((q)_b(q)_{a-b})$ for $0\le b\le a$ and $0$ otherwise.

For an integer triple $\mu=(\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3)$ with $\mu_i\ge0$ and a triple $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3)\in\mathbb Z^3_{\ge0}$ with $|\mu|=|\lambda|$, let the (completely antisymmetric) $A_2$ supernomial $T(\mu;\lambda)$ be the finite sum over chains of Young diagrams encoded by Gaussian $q$-binomials in the standard way (a Kostka-type generating function which is nonzero exactly when $\mu$ dominates the conjugate partition associated to $\lambda$).

For $L=(L_1,L_2)\in\mathbb Z^2_{\ge0}$ and $k=(k_1,k_2,k_3)\in\mathbb Z^3$ with $k_1+k_2+k_3=0$, define the normalized $A_2$ supernomial
$$S(L,k)=\frac{1}{(q)_{CL}}\, T\big((CL)_+;\, L_2(1,1,1)-k\big),$$
where the antisymmetric supernomial with top vector $CL$ and lower vector $L_2(1,1,1)-k$ is meant. Restrict $k$ to the dominant chamber $k_1\ge k_2\ge k_3$, and parametrize it by $K=(K_1,K_2)=(k_1+k_2,\,k_1)$. Then $S(L,K)\ne0$ exactly when
$$K_1\le L_1,\ K_2\le L_2,\ 2K_1\ge K_2,\ 2K_2\ge K_1,\ 2L_1\ge L_2,\ 2L_2\ge L_1.$$

Find an explicit closed-form expression $\bar S(K,L)$ such that, simultaneously,
$$\sum_{L_1,L_2\ge0}\bar S(K,L)\,S(L,K')=\delta_{K,K'}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\sum_{\substack{k\text{ dominant}\\|k|=0}}S(L,k)\,\bar S(k,L')=\delta_{L,L'},$$
valid for all admissible $K=(K_1,K_2)$ (not only for the previously known partial cases $K=(r,2r-p)$ with $p\in\{0,1,2,3\}$).
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on the $A_2$ Bailey lemma and supernomial coefficients explicitly list the $A_2$ supernomial inversion formula as an unsolved problem, with only partial cases known. Recent work on $A_2$ Bailey lemmas and Rogers–Ramanujan-type identities cites this inversion question as still open, and no general closed formula has been published.
